HUMILITY

BY
REV. Andrew Murray

PREFACE.

There are three great motives that urge us to humility. It becomes me
as a creature, as a sinner, as a saint.

In our ordinary religious teaching, the second aspect has been too
exclusively put in the foreground.



Contents

Humility:
I.   '' The Glory of the Creature
II.  '' In the Teaching of Jesus
Notes



Humility: The Beauty of Holiness.

I.

Humility: The Glory of the Creature

_'They shall cast their crowns before the throne, saying: Worthy art
Thou, our Lord and our God. '_--REV. iv. 11.

WHEN God created the universe, it was with the one object of making
the creature partaker of His perfection.

And so pride, or the loss of this humility, is the root of every sin.
'I seek _not_ Mine own will' (John v 30). (See Note A.)



Humility: The Beauty of Holiness

II.

Humility in the Teaching of Jesus.

_'Learn of Me, for I am meek and lowly of heart.'_--MATT. xi. 29.
_'Whosoever will be chief among you, let him be your servant.'_
--MATT. xx. 27.

WE have seen humility in the life of Christ, as He laid open His
heart to us. [Footnote: I knew Jesus, and He was very
precious.'--GEORGE FOXE.]

Once again I repeat what I have said before.[Footnote1: ME is a most
exacting personage.] In their spiritual history men may have had
times of great humbling.

He speaks to us: 'I dwell in the high and holy place, and with him the
is of a contrite and humble spirit.' Be this our portion!



Notes.

NOTE A--'All this is to make it known the region of eternity that
_pride_ can degrade the highest angels into devils.'--_Spirit of
Prayer_, Pt. II. p. 73.


Note B.--'We need to know two things: 1. That our salvation consists
wholly in being saved from _ourselves_.'--W. Law.


A PRAYER FOR HUMILITY

I will here give you an infallible touchstone, that will try all to
the truth.
